newsitem.title: DENMARK: Danish dislike of EMU, EU integration, grows - poll.
newsitem.headline: Danish dislike of EMU, EU integration, grows - poll.

text.p: Danish resistance to economic and monetary union and other European projects has mainly firmed since the Amsterdam summit revised the EU treaty, with most voters undecided on the accord itself, a poll said on Sunday.

A Gallup survey of 1,027 respondents published in the daily Berlingske Tidende showed that 50 percent opposed Danish EMU membership and 42 percent were in favour, compared to 49 percent against and 41 percent for monetary union in a March 1997 poll.
The percentage of undecided voters shrank to eight percent in June from 10 percent in May.
Asked if they would vote to ratify the newly-revised treaty, 45 percent did not know, 34 percent said yes and 21 one percent said that they would oppose ratification.
Prime Minister Poul Nyrup Rasmussen said after the summit on Wednesday that he would hold a referendum on the new accord some time in 1998.
A binding 1993 referendum took Denmark out of EMU and joint defence, citizenship and asylum agreements; a new plebiscite would be required to overturn the decision.

Sunday's Gallup poll showed 46 percent of respondents in favour of dropping the defence optout and 43 percent against, but support for pan-European defence was sharply down from the March survey, where 50 percent wanted to reverse the optout and only 37 percent wanted to retain it.
On asylum policy 46 percent wanted to stay out of joint action and 40 percent to take part, compared to 43 percent and 44 percent respectively in March.
On common citizenship, the number of opponents was unchanged at 73 percent but supporters grew from 14 percent to 15 percent.
